blindSummary:
This state/province applies religious criminal law as part of the twelve-state/province religious-law bloc, adopted by 2002. The religious-law layer criminalises conduct beyond the federal prohibition law — including same-sex acts between women — and religious-law courts hold criminal jurisdiction over adherents of the state religion, residents and visitors alike. No trans-specific incident or documented religious morality-police activity appears in the record for this state/province. Reporting-decay caveats apply: absence of records reflects fear of outing and surveillance gaps, not absence of risk.

Its practical position matches the generic religious-law tier of six further states/provinces: the enacted parallel criminal system itself is the deviation, without additional case-level or enforcement evidence to worsen it further — in contrast to two religious-law states/provinces where capital-penalty text or carried-out capital sentences respectively are on record.
